data.content_ref: inline:SRC_002's central concession — that same-engine execution counts as genuine verification even without engine separation — is undermined by its own analogy/disanalogy: it admits an LLM has a learned prior so self-checking 'may be contaminated,' yet never specifies what evidence within a single run's record would rule out such contamination for same-engine execution. The problem explicitly asks what record-internal evidence distinguishes genuine independent verification from mere restatement; for same-engine execution, SRC_002 only offers 'exact inputs, code, output observed,' but these are present even when the engine's prior steered the code toward a self-confirming bug, so the record cannot distinguish genuine verification from a systematic same-engine confound. Its countercondition acknowledges this gap yet leaves it as an unobserved 'if,' so the argument fails to meet the problem's evidentiary standard for the very case it defends.
